original_question: Let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^3, let Sigma be an orientable smooth two-dimensional surface compactly contained in Omega with simple closed boundary, and interpret Sigma as an insulating crack. For each prescribed boundary current density psi on ∂Omega with zero average, let u solve Delta u = 0 in Omega \ Sigma, with normal derivative grad u · nu = 0 on either side of Sigma and grad u · nu = psi on ∂Omega. Do there exist finitely many boundary current profiles psi_1, ..., psi_N such that, if u_1, ..., u_N are the corresponding potentials, the boundary measurements u_1|_{∂Omega}, ..., u_N|_{∂Omega} uniquely determine Sigma?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1 ("The insulating crack problem") in the arXiv version; the same statement appears as Section 5, Problem 5.1 in the published PDF, p. 595. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper's intended setup: Ω is a bounded connected open subset of R^3; Σ is an orientable smooth two-dimensional surface compactly contained in Ω with simple closed boundary; Σ is interpreted as an insulating crack; the forward problem is the Laplace equation in Ω\Σ with zero normal flux on the two faces of Σ and prescribed zero-average current density ψ on ∂Ω; and the inverse question is whether finitely many boundary measurements corresponding to finitely many chosen current profiles determine Σ. This is very close to the paper's official formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))
missing_details: The paper's quantifiers are a priori: one seeks an integer N and current profiles ψ1, ..., ψN chosen in advance, not depending on the unknown crack Σ. This should be stated explicitly to make the question fully stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))

Because the forward problem is purely Neumann-type, the potential u is only determined up to an additive constant. So the boundary data u_i|_{∂Ω} should be understood either modulo constants or after imposing a normalization; the paper leaves this implicit when it writes both u_i|_{∂Ω} and the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map N_Σ : ψ ↦ u|_{∂Ω}. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

To make 'uniquely determine Σ' fully precise, the comparison quantifier should be spelled out: if two admissible cracks Σ1 and Σ2 give the same measured boundary traces for all chosen ψ_i, then Σ1 = Σ2. This is implicit in the paper's wording but not written out in your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))

The paper explicitly says the boundary value problem is to be interpreted in a weak sense. Your draft states the PDE classically, so adding the weak-solution interpretation makes it more paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))

The nearby context shows the intended scope: planar cracks already have finite-data uniqueness results, while for general curved cracks uniqueness is only known from the full Neumann-to-Dirichlet map. That context should guide the refined question so it stays narrowly about finite-data uniqueness for general smooth cracks, not about broader reconstruction or stability issues. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
refined_question: Given a bounded connected open set Ω ⊂ R^3, does there exist an integer N ≥ 1 and zero-mean boundary current densities ψ1, ..., ψN on ∂Ω, chosen a priori and independently of the unknown crack, such that for every orientable smooth two-dimensional surface Σ compactly contained in Ω and having a simple closed curve as boundary, if u_i^Σ is a weak solution, defined up to an additive constant, of Δu_i^Σ = 0 in Ω\Σ, ∂_ν u_i^Σ = 0 on the two faces of Σ, and ∂_ν u_i^Σ = ψ_i on ∂Ω, then the finite collection of boundary traces u_1^Σ|_{∂Ω}, ..., u_N^Σ|_{∂Ω} (under a common normalization, or modulo additive constants) uniquely determines Σ; equivalently, if two admissible cracks Σ1 and Σ2 produce the same boundary traces on ∂Ω for all i = 1, ..., N, must one have Σ1 = Σ2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))
justification: The nearest official target is the paper's insulating-crack open problem, stated immediately after the forward boundary value problem for u. Your draft is already an expanded near-verbatim version of that problem. The only substantive refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone and faithful are: making the a priori quantifier on the chosen currents explicit; making the uniqueness comparison between two admissible cracks explicit; and accounting for the additive-constant ambiguity inherent in the Neumann problem. The surrounding sentences on the same page confirm that the paper's intent is specifically a finite-data uniqueness question for general smooth cracks, contrasted with earlier planar finite-data results and with curved-crack uniqueness from the full Neumann-to-Dirichlet map. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2003.11441))
